subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram provider intermittently stalls despite stable direct Bot API connectivity

question: Should the remaining Telegram SOCKS5 stall be solved by changing the shared proxy transport contract for explicit and env proxy modes, or should this stay open until live proof narrows the proxy/fallback behavior?
rationale: Source and Undici contract inspection make the proxy failure plausible, but the repair affects shared proxy semantics and the existing candidate PR is partial and unproven.

options.title: Adopt shared scheme-aware proxy repair
options.body: Use the open proxy PR as a starting point or replace it with a shared fix that covers explicit and env SOCKS/HTTP/HTTPS modes plus live Telegram proof.

options.title: Wait for live affected-host proof
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a current-main redacted Telegram SOCKS5 getMe/sendMessage run before choosing code changes.

options.title: Treat as documented operator workaround
options.body: Keep current proxy behavior and document supported DNS/proxy workarounds if maintainers decide the code-level proxy contract should not change without stronger evidence.

recommendation.title: Adopt shared scheme-aware proxy repair
recommendation.body: Use the open proxy PR as a starting point or replace it with a shared fix that covers explicit and env SOCKS/HTTP/HTTPS modes plus live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses Telegram transport and the shared Undici proxy helper history where steipete has the strongest recent routing signal.
